sanskrit: sumālinaṃ hataṃ dṛṣṭvā vasunā bhasmasātkṛtam vidrutaṃ cāpi svaṃ sainyaṃ lakṣayitvārditaṃ śaraiḥ
english: Seeing Sumālin slain and reduced to ashes by the divine weapon, and beholding his own army scattered and tormented by arrows,

sanskrit: tataḥ sa balavān kruddho rāvaṇasya suto yudhi nivartya rākṣasān sarvān meghanādo vyatiṣṭhata
english: then that mighty and wrathful son of Rāvaṇa, Meghanāda, turned all the rākṣasas back and took his stand in battle.

sanskrit: sa rathenāgnivarṇena kāmagena mahārathaḥ abhidudrāva senāṃ tāṃ vanāny agnir iva jvalan
english: That great chariot-warrior charged against that army in a fire-coloured, wish-swift chariot, blazing like a fire consuming forests.

sanskrit: tataḥ praviśatas tasya vividhāyudhadhāriṇaḥ vidudruvur diśaḥ sarvā devās tasya ca darśanāt
english: As he entered bearing all manner of weapons, the gods fled in every direction at the mere sight of him.

sanskrit: na tatrāvasthitaḥ kaś cid raṇe tasya yuyutsataḥ sarvān āvidhya vitrastān dṛṣṭvā śakro 'bhyabhāṣata
english: None remained to face him in battle as he came thirsting to fight; seeing all of them frightened and reeling, Indra spoke.

sanskrit: na bhetavyaṃ na gantavyaṃ nivartadhvaṃ raṇaṃ prati eṣa gacchati me putro yuddhārtham aparājitaḥ
english: "Do not be afraid, do not flee — turn back to the battle. My own son goes forth to fight against this unvanquished one."

sanskrit: tataḥ śakrasuto devo jayanta iti viśrutaḥ rathenādbhutakalpena saṃgrāmam abhivartata
english: Then the divine son of Indra, renowned as Jayanta, advanced toward the battle in a chariot of wondrous make.

sanskrit: tatas te tridaśāḥ sarve parivārya śacīsutam rāvaṇasya sutaṃ yuddhe samāsādya vyavasthitāḥ
english: Then all the thirty gods surrounded the son of Śacī and drew up in array to engage the son of Rāvaṇa in battle.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ yuddhaṃ mahad abhūt sadṛśaṃ devarakṣasām kṛte mahendraputrasya rākṣasendrasutasya ca
english: A great battle ensued, fitting between gods and rākṣasas, centred on the son of Mahendra and the son of the rākṣasa lord.

sanskrit: tato mātaliputre tu gomukhe rākṣasātmajaḥ sārathau pātayām āsa śarān kāñcanabhūṣaṇān
english: Then the rākṣasa's son rained gold-adorned arrows upon Gomukha, the son of Mātali, who was serving as charioteer.

sanskrit: śacīsutas tv api tathā jayantas tasya sārathim taṃ caiva rāvaṇiṃ kruddhaḥ pratyavidhyad raṇājire
english: But Jayanta, son of Śacī, equally enraged, pierced his charioteer and Rāvaṇi himself on the battlefield.

sanskrit: tataḥ kruddho mahātejā rakṣo visphāritekṣaṇaḥ rāvaṇiḥ śakraputraṃ taṃ śaravarṣair avākirat
english: Then that great-spirited rākṣasa Rāvaṇi, enraged and eyes blazing wide, overwhelmed Indra's son with a torrent of arrows.

sanskrit: tataḥ pragṛhya śastrāṇi sāravanti mahānti ca śataghnīs tomarān prāsān gadākhaḍgaparaśvadhān sumahānty adriśṛṅgāṇi pātayām āsa rāvaṇiḥ
english: Then Rāvaṇi seized mighty, potent weapons — śataghnīs, lances, javelins, maces, swords, axes — and hurled enormous mountain peaks as well.

sanskrit: tataḥ pravyathitā lokāḥ saṃjajñe ca tamo mahat tasya rāvaṇaputrasya tadā śatrūn abhighnataḥ
english: Then the worlds were overwhelmed with anguish and a great darkness arose as Rāvaṇa's son struck down his foes.

sanskrit: tatas tad daivatabalaṃ samantāt taṃ śacīsutam bahuprakāram asvasthaṃ tatra tatra sma dhāvati
english: Then the host of gods, distressed in many ways, ran hither and thither surrounding Śacī's son.

sanskrit: nābhyajānaṃs tadānyonyaṃ śatrūn vā daivatāni vā tatra tatra viparyastaṃ samantāt paridhāvitam
english: They could not distinguish one another — neither foe from god — as all was confusion everywhere, with all running about on every side.

sanskrit: etasminn antare śūraḥ pulomā nāma vīryavān daiteyas tena saṃgṛhya śacīputro 'pavāhitaḥ
english: Meanwhile a mighty Daitya named Pulomā, powerful and heroic, seized him and carried Śacī's son away from battle.

sanskrit: gṛhītvā taṃ tu naptāraṃ praviṣṭaḥ sa mahodadhim mātāmaho 'ryakas tasya paulomī yena sā śacī
english: Taking his grandson, he entered the great ocean — he was the maternal grandfather Āryaka, from whose line came Paulomī, the Śacī.

sanskrit: praṇāśaṃ dṛśya tu surā jayantasyātidāruṇam vyathitāś cāprahṛṣṭāś ca samantād vipradudruvuḥ
english: Seeing the exceedingly terrible disappearance of Jayanta, the gods, afflicted and joyless, fled in all directions.

sanskrit: rāvaṇis tv atha saṃhṛṣṭo balaiḥ parivṛtaḥ svakaiḥ abhyadhāvata devāṃs tān mumoca ca mahāsvanam
english: Rāvaṇi, greatly elated and surrounded by his own forces, charged at those gods and let out a tremendous roar.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā praṇāśaṃ putrasya rāvaṇeś cāpi vikramam mātaliṃ prāha devendro rathaḥ samupanīyatām
english: Seeing his son's disappearance and Rāvaṇa's valour, the lord of gods said to Mātali: "Bring the chariot here."

sanskrit: sa tu divyo mahābhīmaḥ sajja eva mahārathaḥ upasthito mātalinā vāhyamāno manojavaḥ
english: That divine, most formidable great chariot, swift as thought, was at the ready, brought forward by Mātali.

sanskrit: tato meghā rathe tasmiṃs taḍidvanto mahāsvanāḥ agrato vāyucapalā gacchanto vyanadaṃs tadā
english: Then clouds with lightning and great thunder moved before that chariot, fickle as the wind, resounding as they went.

sanskrit: nānāvādyāni vādyanta stutayaś ca samāhitāḥ nanṛtuś cāpsaraḥsaṃghāḥ prayāte vāsave raṇam
english: Various instruments were played, hymns of praise were intoned with concentration, and hosts of apsarases danced as Vāsava set forth to battle.

sanskrit: rudrair vasubhir ādityaiḥ sādhyaiś ca samarudgaṇaiḥ vṛto nānāpraharaṇair niryayau tridaśādhipaḥ
english: Attended by Rudras, Vasus, Ādityas, Sādhyas, and the Marud hosts bearing manifold weapons, the lord of the thirty gods issued forth.

sanskrit: nirgacchatas tu śakrasya paruṣaṃ pavano vavau bhāskaro niṣprabhaś cāsīn maholkāś ca prapedire
english: As Indra went forth, a harsh wind blew, the sun grew dim, and great meteors fell.

sanskrit: etasminn antare śūro daśagrīvaḥ pratāpavān āruroha rathaṃ divyaṃ nirmitaṃ viśvakarmaṇā
english: Meanwhile the heroic and splendid Daśagrīva, full of power, mounted the divine chariot fashioned by Viśvakarmā.

sanskrit: pannagaiḥ sumahākāyair veṣṭitaṃ lomaharṣaṇaiḥ yeṣāṃ niśvāsavātena pradīptam iva saṃyugam
english: It was entwined with great-bodied serpents whose very breath made the battle seem ablaze, causing the hair to stand on end.

sanskrit: daityair niśācaraiḥ śūrai rathaḥ saṃparivāritaḥ samarābhimukho divyo mahendram abhivartata
english: That divine chariot, surrounded by heroic Daityas and night-wanderers, faced the battlefield and advanced toward Mahendra.

sanskrit: putraṃ taṃ vārayitvāsau svayam eva vyavasthitaḥ so 'pi yuddhād viniṣkramya rāvaṇiḥ samupāviśat
english: Restraining his son, Rāvaṇa himself took position; and Rāvaṇi, withdrawing from battle, sat down to rest.

sanskrit: tato yuddhaṃ pravṛttaṃ tu surāṇāṃ rākṣasaiḥ saha śastrābhivarṣaṇaṃ ghoraṃ meghānām iva saṃyuge
english: Then began the battle of gods against rākṣasas, a terrible downpour of weapons in combat, like clouds in the monsoon.

sanskrit: kumbhakarṇas tu duṣṭātmā nānāpraharaṇodyataḥ nājñāyata tadā yuddhe saha kenāpy ayudhyata
english: But Kumbhakarṇa, that evil-souled one, wielding all manner of weapons, was not recognized in battle as he fought with any and all.

sanskrit: dantair bhujābhyāṃ padbhyāṃ ca śaktitomarasāyakaiḥ yena kenaiva saṃrabdhas tāḍayām āsa vai surān
english: With teeth, arms, feet, lances, javelins, and arrows, enraged against anyone at all, he battered the gods.

sanskrit: tato rudrair mahābhāgaiḥ sahādityair niśācaraḥ prayuddhas taiś ca saṃgrāme kṛttaḥ śastrair nirantaram
english: Then that night-roamer fought together with the great and glorious Rudras and Ādityas, and was cut without cease by their weapons in the battle.

sanskrit: tatas tad rākṣasaṃ sainyaṃ tridaśaiḥ samarudgaṇaiḥ raṇe vidrāvitaṃ sarvaṃ nānāpraharaṇaiḥ śitaiḥ
english: Then that entire rākṣasa army was routed in battle by the thirty gods together with the Marud troops, with sharp and manifold weapons.

sanskrit: ke cid vinihatāḥ śastrair veṣṭanti sma mahītale vāhaneṣv avasaktāś ca sthitā evāpare raṇe
english: Some, struck down by weapons, writhed on the ground; others, still clinging to their mounts, stood in battle.

sanskrit: rathān nāgān kharān uṣṭrān pannagāṃs turagāṃs tathā śiṃśumārān varāhāṃś ca piśācavadanāṃs tathā
english: Chariots, elephants, donkeys, camels, serpents, horses, dolphins, boars, and those with piśāca-faces —

sanskrit: tān samāliṅgya bāhubhyāṃ viṣṭabdhāḥ ke cid ucchritāḥ devais tu śastrasaṃviddhā mamrire ca niśācaraḥ
english: — some night-wanderers, struck through by the gods' weapons, died clinging to them with their arms, raised up stiffly.

sanskrit: citrakarma ivābhāti sa teṣāṃ raṇasaṃplavaḥ nihatānāṃ pramattānāṃ rākṣasānāṃ mahītale
english: That tumult of battle among those rākṣasas slain and fallen senseless on the earth appeared like a vivid painting.

sanskrit: śoṇitodaka niṣyandākaṅkagṛdhrasamākulā pravṛttā saṃyugamukhe śastragrāhavatī nadī
english: A river flowing at the van of battle ran thick with blood, filled with herons and vultures, bearing away the weapons.

sanskrit: etasminn antare kruddho daśagrīvaḥ pratāpavān nirīkṣya tad balaṃ sarvaṃ daivatair vinipātitam
english: Meanwhile the wrathful and mighty Daśagrīva, beholding his entire army cast down by the gods,

sanskrit: sa taṃ prativigāhyāśu pravṛddhaṃ sainyasāgaram tridaśān samare nighnañ śakram evābhyavartata
english: plunging swiftly into that swelling ocean of armies, slaying the thirty gods in battle, advanced directly against Indra.

sanskrit: tataḥ śakro mahac cāpaṃ visphārya sumahāsvanam yasya visphāraghoṣeṇa svananti sma diśo daśa
english: Then Indra drew his great bow with an immense twang, whose resounding vibration made the ten directions ring.

sanskrit: tad vikṛṣya mahac cāpam indro rāvaṇamūrdhani nipātayām āsa śarān pāvakādityavarcasaḥ
english: Drawing that great bow fully, Indra rained down upon Rāvaṇa's head arrows blazing with the brilliance of fire and sun.

sanskrit: tathaiva ca mahābāhur daśagrīvo vyavasthitaḥ śakraṃ kārmukavibhraṣṭaiḥ śaravarṣair avākirat
english: And likewise the long-armed Daśagrīva, firmly planted, overwhelmed Indra with torrents of arrows released from his bow.

sanskrit: prayudhyator atha tayor bāṇavarṣaiḥ samantataḥ nājñāyata tadā kiṃ cit sarvaṃ hi tamasā vṛtam
english: As the two of them fought, raining arrows on every side, nothing could be distinguished — all was enveloped in darkness.

sanskrit: tatas tamasi saṃjāte rākṣasā daivataiḥ saha ayudhyanta balonmattāḥ sūdayantaḥ parasparam
english: Then, in that darkness that arose, the rākṣasas and gods together fought, intoxicated with power, slaughtering one another.

sanskrit: tatas tu devasainyena rākṣasānāṃ mahad balam daśāṃśaṃ sthāpitaṃ yuddhe śeṣaṃ nītaṃ yamakṣayam
english: Then the divine army left a tenth of the rākṣasa host standing in the battle; the remainder was sent to Yama's realm.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tu tamasā naddhe sarve te devarākṣasāḥ anyonyaṃ nābhyajānanta yudhyamānāḥ parasparam
english: Bound in that darkness, all those gods and rākṣasas could not recognise one another as they fought each other.

sanskrit: indraś ca rāvaṇaś caiva rāvaṇiś ca mahābalaḥ tasmiṃs tamojālavṛte moham īyur na te trayaḥ
english: Indra, Rāvaṇa, and the immensely powerful Rāvaṇi — these three alone did not fall into confusion, even enveloped in the net of darkness.

sanskrit: sa tu dṛṣṭvā balaṃ sarvaṃ nihataṃ rāvaṇo raṇe krodham abhyāgamat tīvraṃ mahānādaṃ ca muktavān
english: Seeing his entire army slain in battle, Rāvaṇa was seized with intense rage and let out a great roar.

sanskrit: krodhāt sūtaṃ ca durdharṣaḥ syandanastham uvāca ha parasainyasya madhyena yāvadantaṃ nayasva mām
english: In his rage, that formidable one spoke to his charioteer seated in the car: "Drive me to the very end, straight through the enemy's army."

sanskrit: adyaitāṃs tridaśān sarvān vikramaiḥ samare svayam nānāśastrair mahāsārair nāśayāmi nabhastalāt
english: "Today by my own valour in battle I shall destroy from the sky all these thirty gods with great, manifold weapons."

sanskrit: aham indraṃ vadhiṣyāmi varuṇaṃ dhanadaṃ yamam tridaśān vinihatyāśu svayaṃ sthāsyāmy athopari
english: "I will slay Indra, Varuṇa, Dhana-da, and Yama; having swiftly destroyed the thirty gods, I myself shall stand above."

sanskrit: viṣādo na ca kartavyaḥ śīghraṃ vāhaya me ratham dviḥ khalu tvāṃ bravīmy adya yāvadantaṃ nayasva mām
english: "There is no room for despondency — drive my chariot quickly. I say it to you twice: drive me to the very end today."

sanskrit: ayaṃ sa nandanoddeśo yatra vartāmahe vayam naya mām adya tatra tvam udayo yatra parvataḥ
english: "This region where we now stand is the Nandana grove; drive me today to where Mount Udaya lies."

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā turagān sa manojavān ādideśātha śatrūṇāṃ madhyenaiva ca sārathiḥ
english: Hearing those words, the charioteer directed the mind-swift horses and drove right through the midst of the enemies.

sanskrit: tasya taṃ niścayaṃ jñātvā śakro deveśvaras tadā rathasthaḥ samarasthāṃs tān devān vākyam athābravīt
english: Understanding his resolve, Indra, lord of the gods, then standing in his chariot, spoke these words to the gods arrayed in battle.

sanskrit: surāḥ śṛṇuta madvākyaṃ yat tāvan mama rocate jīvann eva daśagrīvaḥ sādhu rakṣo nigṛhyatām
english: "Gods, hear my words — this is what pleases me: let the rākṣasa Daśagrīva be subdued while still alive."

sanskrit: eṣa hy atibalaḥ sainye rathena pavanaujasā gamiṣyati pravṛddhormiḥ samudra iva parvaṇi
english: "For this one of surpassing strength will move through the army with the speed of the wind in his chariot, like a swelling ocean at full tide."

sanskrit: na hy eṣa hantuṃ śakyo 'dya varadānāt sunirbhayaḥ tad grahīṣyāmahe rakṣo yattā bhavata saṃyuge
english: "This one cannot be slain today, being utterly fearless by boon of a blessing; therefore we shall seize the rākṣasa — be alert in combat."

sanskrit: yathā baliṃ nigṛhyaitat trailokyaṃ bhujyate mayā evam etasya pāpasya nigraho mama rocate
english: "Just as I enjoy the three worlds by subduing Bali, so it pleases me to subdue this wicked one."

sanskrit: tato 'nyaṃ deśam āsthāya śakraḥ saṃtyajya rāvaṇam ayudhyata mahātejā rākṣasān nāśayan raṇe
english: Then Indra, of great splendour, abandoning Rāvaṇa, took position elsewhere and fought on, destroying rākṣasas in battle.

sanskrit: uttareṇa daśagrīvaḥ praviveśānivartitaḥ dakṣiṇena tu pārśvena praviveśa śatakratuḥ
english: Daśagrīva entered from the north, advancing without turning back; Indra of a hundred sacrifices entered from the southern flank.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa yojanaśataṃ praviṣṭo rākṣasādhipaḥ devatānāṃ balaṃ kṛtsnaṃ śaravarṣair avākirat
english: Then the lord of rākṣasas, having advanced a hundred yojanas, overwhelmed the entire divine army with torrents of arrows.

sanskrit: tataḥ śakro nirīkṣyātha praviṣṭaṃ taṃ balaṃ svakam nyavartayad asaṃbhrāntaḥ samāvṛtya daśānanam
english: Then Indra, observing his own army penetrated, unperturbed, turned it back, surrounding the ten-faced one.

sanskrit: etasminn antare nādo mukto dānavarākṣasaiḥ hā hatāḥ smeti taṃ dṛṣṭvā grastaṃ śakreṇa rāvaṇam
english: Meanwhile a cry went up from the Dānava and rākṣasa troops: "Alas, we are slain!" — seeing Rāvaṇa encircled by Indra.

sanskrit: tato rathaṃ samāruhya rāvaṇiḥ krodhamūrchitaḥ tat sainyam atisaṃkruddhaḥ praviveśa sudāruṇam
english: Then Rāvaṇi, swooning with rage, mounted his chariot and, most furiously angry, entered that terrible army.

sanskrit: sa tāṃ praviśya māyāṃ tu dattāṃ gopatinā purā adṛśyaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ tat sainyaṃ samavākirat
english: Having entered and employing the māyā formerly bestowed by Gopati, invisible to all beings, he rained missiles upon that army.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa devān saṃtyajya śakram evābhyayād drutam mahendraś ca mahātejā na dadarśa sutaṃ ripoḥ
english: Then he abandoned the gods and rushed swiftly against Indra alone; and Mahendra of great splendour could not see the enemy's son.

sanskrit: sa mātaliṃ hayāṃś caiva tāḍayitvā śarottamaiḥ mahendraṃ bāṇavarṣeṇa śīghrahasto hy avākirat
english: That swift-handed one struck Mātali and the horses with excellent arrows and overwhelmed Mahendra with a flood of shafts.

sanskrit: tataḥ śakro rathaṃ tyaktva visṛjya ca sa mātalim airāvataṃ samāruhya mṛgayām āsa rāvaṇim
english: Then Indra, abandoning the chariot and releasing Mātali, mounted Airāvata and sought out Rāvaṇi.

sanskrit: sa tu māyā balād rakṣaḥ saṃgrāme nābhyadṛśyata kiramāṇaḥ śaraughena mahendram amitaujasaḥ
english: But that rākṣasa, by the power of māyā, was not visible in battle, pouring streams of arrows upon Mahendra, whose energy is unbounded.

sanskrit: sa taṃ yadā pariśrāntam indraṃ mene 'tha rāvaṇiḥ tadainaṃ māyayā baddhvā svasainyam abhito 'nayat
english: When Rāvaṇi judged Indra to be exhausted, he bound him by māyā and brought him right to his own army.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvātha balāt tasmin māyayāpahṛtaṃ raṇe mahendram amarāḥ sarve kiṃ nv etad iti cukruśuḥ na hi dṛśyati vidyāvān māyayā yena nīyate
english: Seeing Mahendra thus forcibly seized in battle and carried off by māyā, all the immortals cried out: "What is this?" — for the wielder of māyā by whom he was being led could not be seen.

sanskrit: etasminn antare cāpi sarve suragaṇās tadā abhyadravan susaṃkruddhā rāvaṇaṃ śastravṛṣṭibhiḥ
english: Meanwhile all the hosts of gods, utterly enraged, rushed upon Rāvaṇa with showers of weapons.

sanskrit: rāvaṇas tu samāsādya vasvādityamarudgaṇān na śaśāka raṇe sthātuṃ na yoddhuṃ śastrapīḍitaḥ
english: But Rāvaṇa, encountering the Vasus, Ādityas, and Marud hosts, could neither stand in battle nor fight, tormented by their weapons.

sanskrit: taṃ tu dṛṣṭvā pariśrāntaṃ prahārair jarjaracchavim rāvaṇiḥ pitaraṃ yuddhe 'darśanastho 'bravīd idam
english: Seeing his father exhausted, his body broken by blows, Rāvaṇi, standing invisible in battle, spoke these words to him:

sanskrit: āgaccha tāta gacchāvo nivṛttaṃ raṇakarma tat jitaṃ te viditaṃ bho 'stu svastho bhava gatajvaraḥ
english: "Come, father, let us go — the work of battle is done. Know that you have conquered; be at ease, be free from distress."

sanskrit: ayaṃ hi surasainyasya trailokyasya ca yaḥ prabhuḥ sa gṛhīto mayā śakro bhagnamānāḥ surāḥ kṛtāḥ
english: "For I have seized Indra, the master of the divine army and of the three worlds; the gods have been broken in spirit."

sanskrit: yatheṣṭaṃ bhuṅkṣva trailokyaṃ nigṛhya ripum ojasā vṛthā te kiṃ śramaṃ kṛtvā yuddhaṃ hi tava niṣphalam
english: "Enjoy the three worlds at your pleasure, having subdued the foe by might. Why exhaust yourself to no purpose? Your battle is fruitless now."

sanskrit: sa daivatabalāt tasmān nivṛtto raṇakarmaṇaḥ tac chrutvā rāvaṇer vākyaṃ svasthacetā daśānanaḥ
english: Hearing Rāvaṇi's words, Daśagrīva was composed in mind and withdrew from the work of battle against the divine army.

sanskrit: atha raṇavigatajvaraḥ prabhur vijayam avāpya niśācarādhipaḥ bhavanam abhi tato jagāma hṛṣṭaḥ svasutam avāpya ca vākyam abravīt
english: Then the lord, the master of night-roamers, free of battle's anguish and having won victory, departed joyfully for his palace; and meeting his own son, he spoke:

sanskrit: atibalasadṛśaiḥ parākramais tair mama kulamānavivardhanaṃ kṛtam yad amarasamavikrama tvayā tridaśapatis tridaśāś ca nirjitāḥ
english: "By those feats of prowess worthy of supreme strength, the honour of my lineage has been exalted; for you, whose valour rivals the immortals', have defeated the lord of the thirty gods and the thirty gods themselves."

sanskrit: tvaritam upanayasva vāsavaṃ nagaram ito vraja sainyasaṃvṛtaḥ aham api tava gacchato drutaṃ saha sacivair anuyāmi pṛṣṭhataḥ
english: "Bring Vāsava here quickly — go to the city, surrounded by your army; I too shall follow swiftly behind you with my ministers as you proceed."

sanskrit: atha sa balavṛtaḥ savāhanas tridaśapatiṃ parigṛhya rāvaṇiḥ svabhavanam upagamya rākṣaso muditamanā visasarja rākṣasān
english: Then that rākṣasa Rāvaṇi, surrounded by his army and bearing the lord of the thirty gods, went to his own abode; joyful in mind, he dismissed the rākṣasas.

sanskrit: jite mahendre 'tibale rāvaṇasya sutena vai prajāpatiṃ puraskṛtya gatā laṅkāṃ surās tadā
english: When mighty Mahendra had been conquered by Rāvaṇa's son, the gods, placing Prajāpati at their head, went to Laṅkā.

sanskrit: taṃ rāvaṇaṃ samāsādya putrabhrātṛbhir āvṛtam abravīd gagane tiṣṭhan sāntvapūrvaṃ prajāpatiḥ
english: Approaching Rāvaṇa, surrounded by his sons and brothers, Prajāpati stood in the sky and spoke with words of conciliation:

sanskrit: vatsa rāvaṇa tuṣṭo 'smi tava putrasya saṃyuge aho 'sya vikramaudāryaṃ tava tulyo 'dhiko 'pi vā
english: "My dear Rāvaṇa, I am pleased by your son's conduct in battle. How great is his valour and nobility — equal to you, perhaps exceeding you."

sanskrit: jitaṃ hi bhavatā sarvaṃ trailokyaṃ svena tejasā kṛtā pratijñā saphalā prīto 'smi svasutena vai
english: "For all three worlds have been conquered by your energy; the vow has borne fruit; I am pleased by my own son indeed."

sanskrit: ayaṃ ca putro 'tibalas tava rāvaṇarāvaṇiḥ indrajit tv iti vikhyāto jagaty eṣa bhaviṣyati
english: "And this immensely powerful son of yours, Rāvaṇa's Rāvaṇi — he shall be renowned throughout the world as Indrajit, the Conqueror of Indra."

sanskrit: balavāñ śatrunirjetā bhaviṣyaty eṣa rākṣasaḥ yam āśritya tvayā rājan sthāpitās tridaśā vaśe
english: "This rākṣasa shall be mighty, a conqueror of enemies; relying on him, O king, you have brought the thirty gods under your dominion."

sanskrit: tan mucyatāṃ mahābāho mahendraḥ pākaśāsanaḥ kiṃ cāsya mokṣaṇārthāya prayacchanti divaukasaḥ
english: "Therefore let Mahendra, the chastiser of Pāka, be released, O mighty-armed one. And what will the heaven-dwellers give for his release?"

sanskrit: athābravīn mahātejā indrajit samitiṃjayaḥ amaratvam ahaṃ deva vṛṇomīhāsya mokṣaṇe
english: Then great-spirited Indrajit, victorious in battle, spoke: "O god, I choose immortality in exchange for his release."

sanskrit: abravīt tu tadā devo rāvaṇiṃ kamalodbhavaḥ nāsti sarvāmaratvaṃ hi keṣāṃ cit prāṇināṃ bhuvi
english: The lotus-born god then said to Rāvaṇi: "Complete immortality does not exist for any living being on earth."

sanskrit: athābravīt sa tatrastham indrajit padmasaṃbhavam śrūyatāṃ yā bhavet siddhiḥ śatakratuvimokṣaṇe
english: Then Indrajit spoke to the lotus-born god present there: "Hear what attainment shall be mine in exchange for releasing the lord of a hundred sacrifices."

sanskrit: mameṣṭaṃ nityaśo deva havyaiḥ saṃpūjya pāvakam saṃgrāmam avatartuṃ vai śatrunirjayakāṅkṣiṇaḥ
english: "What I desire, O god, is that whenever I descend into battle seeking to conquer enemies, I may first duly propitiate Agni with oblations;"

sanskrit: tasmiṃś ced asamāpte tu japyahome vibhāvasoḥ yudhyeyaṃ deva saṃgrāme tadā me syād vināśanam
english: "and if I should enter battle, O god, with the japa-oblation to Vibhāvasu incomplete, then let that be the occasion of my destruction."

sanskrit: sarvo hi tapasā caiva vṛṇoty amaratāṃ pumān vikrameṇa mayā tv etad amaratvaṃ pravartitam
english: "For every man wins immortality through austerity; but I have established this immortality through valour."

sanskrit: evam astv iti taṃ prāha vākyaṃ devaḥ prajāpatiḥ muktaś cendrajitā śakro gatāś ca tridivaṃ surāḥ
english: "So be it," said the god Prajāpati to him; and Indra was released by Indrajit, and the gods departed to the heavens.

sanskrit: etasminn antare śakro dīno bhraṣṭāmbarasrajaḥ rāma cintāparītātmā dhyānatatparatāṃ gataḥ
english: Meanwhile Indra, dejected, his garments and garlands dishevelled, fell deep into meditation, his mind entirely absorbed in thoughts of Rāma.

sanskrit: taṃ tu dṛṣṭvā tathābhūtaṃ prāha devaḥ prajāpatiḥ śakrakrato kim utkaṇṭhāṃ karoṣi smara duṣkṛtam
english: Seeing him in this state, the god Prajāpati said: "O Indra of a hundred sacrifices, why do you grieve? Recall the wrong you committed."

sanskrit: amarendra mayā bahvyaḥ prajāḥ sṛṣṭāḥ purā prabho ekavarṇāḥ samābhāṣā ekarūpāś ca sarvaśaḥ
english: "O lord of immortals, in the beginning I created many creatures — all of one colour, all speaking alike, all of one form in every respect."

sanskrit: tāsāṃ nāsti viśeṣo hi darśane lakṣaṇe 'pi vā tato 'ham ekāgramanās tāḥ prajāḥ paryacintayam
english: "There was no distinction among them in appearance or in marks; thereupon I, with focused mind, reflected on those creatures."

sanskrit: so 'haṃ tāsāṃ viśeṣārthaṃ striyam ekāṃ vinirmame yad yat prajānāṃ pratyaṅgaṃ viśiṣṭaṃ tat tad uddhṛtam
english: "To create a distinction among them, I fashioned one woman, extracting whatever was the finest feature of each and every creature."

sanskrit: tato mayā rūpaguṇair ahalyā strī vinirmitā ahalyety eva ca mayā tasyā nāma pravartitam
english: "Thus I fashioned the woman Ahalyā from beauties and virtues; and indeed it was I who gave her the name Ahalyā."

sanskrit: nirmitāyāṃ tu devendra tasyāṃ nāryāṃ surarṣabha bhaviṣyatīti kasyaiṣā mama cintā tato 'bhavat
english: "Having fashioned that woman, O lord of gods, O bull among immortals, I then fell to wondering: whose shall she be?"

sanskrit: tvaṃ tu śakra tadā nārīṃ jānīṣe manasā prabho sthānādhikatayā patnī mamaiṣeti puraṃdara
english: "But you, Indra, O lord, O Purandara, claimed that woman in your heart, thinking 'She shall be my wife' on account of your superior station."

sanskrit: sā mayā nyāsabhūtā tu gautamasya mahātmanaḥ nyastā bahūni varṣāṇi tena niryātitā ca sā
english: "She was placed by me in trust with the great-souled Gautama, entrusted for many years; and she was eventually surrendered to him by me."

sanskrit: tatas tasya parijñāya mayā sthairyaṃ mahāmuneḥ jñātvā tapasi siddhiṃ ca patnyarthaṃ sparśitā tadā
english: "Then, having recognised the steadfastness of that great sage and knowing his perfection in austerity, I bestowed her on him as his wife."

sanskrit: sa tayā saha dharmātmā ramate sma mahāmuniḥ āsan nirāśā devās tu gautame dattayā tayā
english: "That righteous great sage dwelt joyfully with her; when she was given to Gautama, the gods lost hope."

sanskrit: tvaṃ kruddhas tv iha kāmātmā gatvā tasyāśramaṃ muneḥ dṛṣṭavāṃś ca tadā tāṃ strīṃ dīptām agniśikhām iva
english: "But you, angry and ruled by lust, went to the hermitage of that sage and saw that woman then blazing like a flame of fire."

sanskrit: sā tvayā dharṣitā śakra kāmārtena samanyunā dṛṣṭas tvaṃ ca tadā tena āśrame paramarṣiṇā
english: "She was violated by you, Indra, overcome with desire and consumed by passion; and you were then seen by that supreme sage in his hermitage."

sanskrit: tataḥ kruddhena tenāsi śaptaḥ paramatejasā gato 'si yena devendra daśābhāgaviparyayam
english: "Then that one of supreme splendour, enraged, cursed you; by that curse, O lord of gods, you underwent a reversal in a tenth part of your body."

sanskrit: yasmān me dharṣitā patnī tvayā vāsava nirbhayam tasmāt tvaṃ samare rājañ śatruhastaṃ gamiṣyasi
english: "'Because you have recklessly violated my wife, O Vāsava, therefore, O king, you shall fall into an enemy's hands in battle.'"

sanskrit: ayaṃ tu bhāvo durbuddhe yas tvayeha pravartitaḥ mānuṣeṣv api sarveṣu bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ
english: "'And this tendency you have set in motion here, O wicked-minded one, will without doubt spread among all human beings as well.'"

sanskrit: tatrādharmaḥ subalavān samutthāsyati yo mahān tatrārdhaṃ tasya yaḥ kartā tvayy ardhaṃ nipatiṣyati
english: "'A great and most powerful adharma will arise there; half of that shall fall upon whoever commits it, and half upon you.'"

sanskrit: na ca te sthāvaraṃ sthānaṃ bhaviṣyati puraṃdara etenādharmayogena yas tvayeha pravartitaḥ
english: "'And you shall have no stable station, O Purandara, by reason of this bond of adharma which you have set in motion here.'"

sanskrit: yaś ca yaś ca surendraḥ syād dhruvaḥ sa na bhaviṣyati eṣa śāpo mayā mukta ity asau tvāṃ tadābravīt
english: "'And whoever becomes a supreme Indra shall not remain permanent in that station.' So saying, he released this curse upon you at that time."

sanskrit: tāṃ tu bhāryāṃ vinirbhartsya so 'bravīt sumahātapāḥ durvinīte vinidhvaṃsa mamāśramasamīpataḥ
english: "And rebuking his wife severely, that one of immense austerity said: 'O undisciplined woman, vanish from the vicinity of my hermitage!'"

sanskrit: rūpayauvanasaṃpannā yasmāt tvam anavasthitā tasmād rūpavatī loke na tvam ekā bhaviṣyasi
english: "'Since you, endowed with beauty and youth, were not constant, therefore in the world you shall not be the only beautiful woman.'"

sanskrit: rūpaṃ ca tat prajāḥ sarvā gamiṣyanti sudurlabham yat tavedaṃ samāśritya vibhrame 'yam upasthitaḥ
english: "'And all creatures shall acquire that beauty — so exceedingly rare — which was the occasion of this transgression of yours.'"

sanskrit: tadā prabhṛti bhūyiṣṭhaṃ prajā rūpasamanvitāḥ śāpotsargād dhi tasyedaṃ muneḥ sarvam upāgatam
english: "From that time on creatures were abundantly endowed with beauty; all this came about through the release of that sage's curse."

sanskrit: tat smara tvaṃ mahābāho duṣkṛtaṃ yat tvayā kṛtam yena tvaṃ grahaṇaṃ śatror gato nānyena vāsava
english: "Remember, O mighty-armed Vāsava, the wrong that you committed — by that, not by anything else, you have fallen into an enemy's grasp."

sanskrit: śīghraṃ yajasva yajñaṃ tvaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ susamāhitaḥ pāvitas tena yajñena yāsyasi tridivaṃ tataḥ
english: "Perform the Vaiṣṇava sacrifice quickly, with focused mind; purified by that sacrifice, you will then ascend to the heavens."

sanskrit: putraś ca tava devendra na vinaṣṭo mahāraṇe nītaḥ saṃnihitaś caiva aryakeṇa mahodadhau
english: "And your son, O lord of gods, has not perished in the great battle; he was carried away and is safely present with Āryaka in the great ocean."

sanskrit: etac chrutvā mahendras tu yajñam iṣṭvā ca vaiṣṇavam punas tridivam ākrāmad anvaśāsac ca devatāḥ
english: Hearing this, Mahendra performed the Vaiṣṇava sacrifice and once again ascended to the heavens, ruling over the gods.

sanskrit: etad indrajito rāma balaṃ yat kīrtitaṃ mayā nirjitas tena devendraḥ prāṇino 'nye ca kiṃ punaḥ
english: "This, O Rāma, is the might of Indrajit that I have recounted to you; by him the lord of gods himself was conquered — what then of other living beings?"
